questions.q: In the example workflow, what does `cron: "0 23 * * MON-FRI"` configure?
options: A schedule that fires the job at 23:00 UTC every weeknight
A manual button that requires a person to click it every night
A rule that disables the workflow on weekends only when combined with workflow_dispatch
A step that checks out the repository code
questions.explain: The cron expression fires the scheduled job at 23:00 UTC on Monday through Friday, with no person needing to trigger it.

questions.q: Why is the `actions/checkout@v4` step needed before the script can run?
options: A hosted runner starts completely empty, so this step pulls the repository's files, including the script, onto it
It installs PowerShell onto the runner for the first time
It automatically fixes any syntax errors in the script
It deletes old versions of the script from Git history
questions.explain: Without checkout, the hosted runner has nothing on it — this step is what makes scripts/Stop-DevVMs.ps1 available to run.

questions.q: Where does the credential used by `azure/login@v2` come from in this workflow?
options: The repository's GitHub Actions secrets, referenced as ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}, never written in the file
A plaintext value typed directly into the YAML file
The personal Azure account of whoever last edited the workflow
It is generated randomly each time the job runs and discarded afterward
questions.explain: The creds value pulls AZURE_CREDENTIALS from the repo's stored secrets, consistent with never hardcoding a credential.

questions.q: What does this workflow actually run, and where did that script originally come from?
options: Stop-DevVMs.ps1, the VM start/stop script built earlier, in Lesson 21 of this course
A brand-new script written for the first time in this lesson
A built-in GitHub Actions command with no custom script involved
An Azure CLI command typed directly into the workflow file
questions.explain: The workflow's run step executes ./scripts/Stop-DevVMs.ps1, the same cost-savings script from Lesson 21, now running on a schedule.

questions.q: What is a service principal, as used by the `azure/login@v2` step?
options: An identity Azure issues for an application or automation to authenticate with, instead of a human user account
A person's personal Azure username and password
A type of virtual machine used only for running pipelines
A GitHub-specific feature unrelated to Azure authentication
questions.explain: A service principal lets automation like this pipeline authenticate to Azure without relying on a human's own credentials.
